newsitem.title: INDIA: India ICICI 96/97 disbursals up 26 pct.
newsitem.headline: India ICICI 96/97 disbursals up 26 pct.

text.p: Disbursals by Indian term lender the Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India (ICICI) stood at a little over 90 billion rupees in financial year 1996/97 (April-March), a company official said on Monday.
"Disbursements were 9,000-odd crores, up 26 percent over last year," ICICI Managing Director K.V. Kamath told reporters on the margins of a news conference.
"Sanctions were about 22 percent higher than disbursals at 11,500 crores," he added.
Kamath said he was targeting disbursals of around 135 billion rupees next year, of which he expected 100 billion rupees would be in the local currency and another 35 billion in foreign exchange.
"As long as approvals are about 20 percent more than disbursals, we're fine," Kamath added. "They will translate into 20 percent growth next year."

Kamath, who is also CEO of ICICI, said almost 20 percent of ICICI's disbursals in 1996/97 went into the infrastructure sector, and he expected this figure to increase to between 33 to 40 percent next year.
"There will be more investment in ports, roads and telecoms," Kamath said.
